title: Dayparted throughput entitlements and smoothing credits for Dedicated customers
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design contract language, measurement and operational controls for a daypart-aware throughput entitlement model that smooths crediting across predictable intra-day traffic patterns. Aim is to give Dedicated customers predictable guaranteed capacity while avoiding punitive credits for short, scheduled bursts (e.g., morning batch windows) and enabling autoscaler interlocks to protect other tenants.
background: Customers with dedicated pools report that rigid per-minute quantile SLAs produce large credit exposures for customers who have highly predictable daily spikes (e.g., 08:00-09:00 ET). Current SLA measurement windows are uniform across the day and charge credits for short-lived breaches, which complicates sales negotiations and increases operational churn. Several recent renewals requested a formal mechanism to recognize scheduled dayparts and to smooth credit allocation over a rolling 24h horizon.
goals: (1) Define daypart-aware entitlement definitions that can be contractually committed; (2) Provide a deterministic credit smoothing algorithm that reduces volatile refunds for predictable bursts; (3) Ensure autoscaler and routing policies respect daypart reservations to avoid cross-customer impact; (4) Produce short, clear contract clauses and an operational runbook.
proposal: Introduce 'dayparts' as an opt-in contract construct: the customer declares up to three recurring daily windows and an expected reserved throughput for each. SLA measurement uses a hybrid windowing approach: per-minute availability is evaluated but credits are computed on a 24-hour rolling 'smoothed breach' score that weights breaches by duration and proximity to declared dayparts. Short, scheduled spikes inside a declared daypart are discounted per the crediting formula. Unscheduled breaches and breaches outside dayparts are weighted normally. Autoscaler interlock will respect declared dayparts by prewarming up to the reserved throughput 10 minutes prior to a daypart when configured.
measurement:
- Input: per-customer per-az token successful serve rate sampled at 1-minute resolution; baseline reserved throughput per daypart; regular (non-daypart) reserved baseline.
- Compute per-minute breach indicator when effective throughput < reserved throughput.
- For crediting: compute weighted_breach_score = sum_over_last_24h(breach_indicator * weight(t)) where weight(t) = 0.2 inside declared short burst windows within daypart (<=10 minutes) and 1.0 outside dayparts or for sustained breach > 10 minutes.
- Translate weighted_breach_score into credit percentage using a calibrated mapping table (example in appendix).
- Metrics exposed in Console: daypart utilization, prewarm activations, weighted_breach_score, raw minute-breach-rate.
- Measurement sources: serving runtime token logs, autoscaler events, route-level throttles.
acceptance_criteria: Contract clause for dayparts drafted and legal-reviewed
Crediting algorithm prototyped and results reproducible on historical traffic for 3 pilot customers
Console exposes daypart config, prewarm toggle, and the four measurement metrics (utilization, prewarm activations, weighted_breach_score, raw_minute_breach_rate)
Autoscaler interlock implements prewarm behavior and honors configured daypart reservation during rollout in a canary to 2 tenants
Billing pipeline emits credit decisions and a human-readable rationale for each credit event
proposed_contract_language: (Short form) 'Customer may designate up to three recurring daily time windows ("dayparts") and an associated reserved throughput for each. Redwood will measure per-minute serve capacity. For the purposes of credit computation, Redwood will apply a 24-hour smoothed crediting method that reduces the weight of short, scheduled bursts occurring wholly within a declared daypart. Credits are calculated from the resulting weighted breach score using the schedule in Appendix A. Designation of dayparts is optional and subject to review; misuse (undisclosed or frequently changing dayparts) may result in rescinding daypart privileges.'
operational_playbook:
- Onboarding: sales collects daypart windows and expected throughput; PM/SE open a configuration ticket.
- Runtime: prewarm triggers 10 minutes before a daypart if prewarm is enabled; operation logs the prewarm event.
- Alerting: create SLO alerts on weighted_breach_score and raw_minute_breach_rate.
- Incident: if weighted_breach_score exceeds threshold, engage capacity runbook; if breach due to autoscaler failure, escalate to infra oncall.
- Credit processing: daily batch computes credits for active dedicated accounts and produces a posterity CSV for Finance and CS.
- Abuse detection: validate declared dayparts against historical traffic; flag if >30% variance for three consecutive cycles.
rollout_plan: 1) Prototype algorithm on historical logs for two pilot customers (2 weeks). 2) Legal and Finance review draft contract language (1 week). 3) Implement Console daypart UI and telemetry (3 sprints). 4) Implement autoscaler prewarm interlock and safe flags (2 sprints). 5) Pilot with 3 customers on opt-in contracts for 6 weeks. 6) Iterate and general release in dedicated-2.8.
technical_requirements:
- Serving runtime must emit per-minute token serve metrics with customer and AZ tags.
- Autoscaler must support timed prewarm actions and reservation pins.
- Billing pipeline must be able to ingest weighted breach scores and map to credit amounts.
- Console must show daypart config and time-series for daypart utilization.
- Feature flags for dayparting must be available per-customer for staged rollout.
risks: Customers may over-declare dayparts to game credits — mitigated by variance monitoring and contractual limits
Complexity in measurement could lead to disputes — mitigated by exposing transparent math and downloadable evidence per credit event
Prewarm traffic could raise costs if misused — mitigated by prewarm caps and optional customer-approved budget caps
Autoscaler edge cases (failed prewarm) may cause transient degradations — mitigated by fallback routing and conservative prewarm sizing
